newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Prices supported amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Prices supported amid tight supplies.

text.p: Spot MTBE prices in Asia were supported amid tight supplies this week, although some erosion could occur heading into March trading, market sources said on Wednesday.
More supplies were expected in March, although traders said sellers will look to account for expensive feedstock costs.

Traders said cargoes for February had been traded within the week as high as $290 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Singapore basis for February lifting, up from $280 per tonne heard last week.
Free-on-board (fob) prices were lower and assessed by traders at $275 to $280 although 1,000 tonnes was reported traded within the week at $270 on an inter-tank transfer (ITT) basis in February.
"It (fob prices) is very hard to gauge because most suppliers are through with February and looking to March," a trader said on Singapore supplies.
But there were some remaining February availabilities in other parts of the region, sources said.
Malaysia was still able to offer small quantities and a seller in South Korea was offering 4,000 tonnes of February MTBE at $270 fob, facing bids at $260-$263, traders said.
One trader did not expect support to last into March with cargoes being shipped in from the Mideast.
Mideast supplies were also due to increase with petrochemical giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) bringing onstream a 700,000-tonne per year MTBE plant sometime in March-April.
But on the other hand, domestic Saudi demand for methanol, a feedstock for the petroleum additive, would increase and reduce export availabilities, boosting prices for the already expensive chemical.
Traders said methanol prices had risen to $235-$240 per tonne c-and-f southeast Asia from around $230 last week. In recent weeks prices have risen by more than $80.
One methanol trader projected prices to keep rising in the first quarter to $260-$270 where it would hold through to the second quarter.
"I don't think it will last long, there should be enough supply by then," he said, referring to new supplies from Chile and the return of a Malaysian plant.
Part of the methanol shortage in Asia has been attributed to the shutdown of the 660,000 tonne per year state-owned Petronas Methanol Labuan plant in East Malaysia.

The whole plant, shutdown since December 26 when storms damaged a boiler, is due back in the first week of February. But the boiler will be replaced sometime in April, which requires a shutdown of 30-35 days.
"It is an opportunistic price for methanol, but MTBE In Asia is not determined by feedstock prices, as much as by demand and supply," said one trader, disagreeing to the high MTBE prices.
With the exception of Taiwan which last week bought through tender two 3,500 tonne cargoes for March 1-15 at $283 per tonne c-and-f, regional demand was lacklustre, he said.
"Let's look to Taiwan's reformate tender which has a two percent oxygenate requirement and see whether that attracts demand," said a trader.

Taiwan's reformate import tender for 250,000 barrels in March 1-15, closed on January 28 with offers valid for two days. On Wednesday afternoon, sources said at least two cargoes would be awarded below $28.00 per barrel c-and-f.
--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3086)
